extra.message: User-controlled 'severity' and 'keyword' query parameters are interpolated directly into a raw SQL string passed to AppDataSource.query(). An attacker can inject SQL (e.g. severity='x' UNION SELECT ...) to read arbitrary data from the database.

spawn() is invoked with shell:true and a string built from the unvalidated req.query.format plus application data, allowing command injection (e.g. format='; rm -rf /') and path traversal. The partner variant validates the format against a whitelist and uses shell:false; this route does neither.

The user-supplied req.query.formula is concatenated into a new Function() body ('with (context) { return (<formula>); }') and executed. This is arbitrary JavaScript code execution (RCE) reachable by any underwriter/admin.

completeAccountVerification accepts an email and token but never validates the token against the stored resetTokenHash. It only checks the account is not disabled and then signs a session. Any unauthenticated caller can impersonate any user (including admin) by supplying their email and an arbitrary 20+ char token.

GET /api/cases/:externalId/timeline is registered before router.use(requireAuth), so it is publicly accessible. It returns internal underwriting notes (body, severity) and decision reasons to unauthenticated callers.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: getUnderwritingNoteDetail loads an UnderwritingNote by ID and returns its full body and severity without any role or ownership check. Any authenticated user, including a borrower, can enumerate note IDs and read internal risk notes (IDOR / broken access control).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: parseWorkspaceEnvelope() expands internal DTD entities and, for SYSTEM entities with a file:// value, calls fs.readFileSync on the path. The value comes from the base64 'lop_workspace_envelope' cookie (via /applications/:id/workspace-envelope), enabling XXE-based arbitrary local file read.

The x-checklist-locale request header is used unvalidated to build a file path (path.join(CHECKLIST_TEMPLATE_DIR, `${locale}.md`)). A value like '../../../../etc/passwd' reads arbitrary files from the server (path traversal / arbitrary file read).

The 'lop_workspace_alias' cookie is used directly as a path component (path.join(WORKING_PAPER_DIR, workspaceAlias)) without validation, allowing path traversal to write markdown files to arbitrary locations.

The marketing asset filename is built from attacker-controlled req.body.slot and req.file.originalname (path.join(marketingAssetsDir, `${slot}-${originalname}`)). originalname is not sanitized, enabling path traversal to write files (including scripts) outside the intended public directory, and there is no content-type restriction.

The 'term' query parameter is interpolated directly into an LDAP filter string (`(&(department=underwriting)(cn=*${term}*))`) without escaping, allowing LDAP filter injection to widen the predicate and enumerate arbitrary directory entries. The sibling route correctly uses escapeDirectoryFilterValue; this one does not.

The export_name query parameter is placed into the Content-Disposition header without stripping CR/LF characters, allowing HTTP response header injection / response splitting. The preview sibling route strips CR/LF; this export route does not.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers

extra.message: The x-partner-document-url header is fetched directly without host validation (unlike the compliance-bulletin sibling which whitelists hosts), allowing SSRF against internal network services from a staff-only endpoint.

restoreReviewerQueuePreferences parses the 'rq_prefs' cookie as JSON and calls Object.assign(user, parsed) before saving. A staff user can set role:'admin' (or disabled:false) in their own cookie to escalate privileges to administrator.

applyIntakeFormUpdate does Object.assign(application, req.body) with the raw request body. A borrower can set arbitrary fields such as status:'approved', riskTier, amount, or decisionSummary on their own application, bypassing the workflow state machine and authorization checks.

jwt.verify is called with algorithms ['HS256','none'], allowing an attacker to forge an unsigned (alg:none) receipt that passes verification and is used to write outbox events referencing arbitrary integrationId/externalId.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: recordPayoutInstruction stores full bank accountNumber and routingNumber in plaintext (unlike the partner variant which encrypts via encryptPayoutDetails), and on error logs the entire body (including those account/routing numbers) to the activity log. Sensitive financial data at rest and in logs.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: provisionPartnerPortalAccount hashes passwords with a single unsalted SHA-256 digest instead of a slow password KDF (bcrypt as used elsewhere). Weak/unsalted hashing leaves credentials vulnerable to offline cracking and rainbow tables.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: On error, generatePortfolioRiskSummary returns the raw error message and stack trace to the client, disclosing internal implementation details and database error information.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The raw 'query' parameter (including newlines) is written directly to the activity log without sanitization, enabling log injection/forgery. The document-search sibling sanitizes CR/LF; this endpoint does not.

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: resolvePartnerIntegrationAccess uses a truthy check (if (result.access)) on a loosely-typed ledger value that may be the string 'false'. A non-empty string is truthy, so even-numbered branch IDs are reported as elevated access, bypassing the intended authorization.

The 'lop_theme_pref' cookie value is reflected unescaped into a <script> tag. A user-controlled cookie value containing '</script><script>...' yields stored/reflected XSS in the workspace theme widget.

completeDocumentUploadFlow redirects to an arbitrary URL taken from the x-redirect-url header or the request body returnTo field without validation, allowing open redirect (used for phishing/token leakage).

A hardcoded fallback JWT secret ('dev-only-change-me-loan-origination-portal') is used whenever JWT_SECRET is not set. If deployed without an environment variable, session tokens can be forged with a publicly known secret.

A hardcoded default public API key ('portal-status-demo-key') is used for the /api/public/status endpoint and is seeded as the integration API key hash. Anyone knowing the default key can access the public status API.
